title: Niska lands rezoning withdrawn; 70 Fountain Street approved
subtitle: Council also advanced a charitable hub exploration, received the 220 Arkell Road report, and designated 65 McTague Street.
overview: Council withdrew its own proposal to redesignate and rezone the 8-hectare southeast parcel of the Niska lands from residential to open space and parkland, and closed the file {{vote:m15}}. A motion to defer the decision until talks with the Province had concluded was defeated {{vote:m13}}. Council will instead write to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, share the public delegations and the City's historical financial contributions, and invite the Province to meet community advocates about a provincial rezoning decision. Staff and the CAO warned of legal and financial risk, and of risk to the City's pending purchase of the former waterfowl park lands.

Council approved a 24-storey rental building at 70 Fountain Street East with amendments on rooftop mechanical height, ground-floor retail area and larger bike parking {{vote:m7}}. It also asked for a public written draft proposal for a possible community hub and affordable housing site in Guelph/Eramosa, to be cost neutral to the City {{vote:m8}}.

Council received the report on the 220 Arkell Road subdivision, a public meeting only {{vote:m9}}, and started the heritage designation process for 65 McTague Street {{vote:m1}}. After a closed session on the Niska item, the mayor reported that council received legal advice and gave no direction.

decisions.detail: Council withdrew the City-initiated official plan and zoning amendments and closed the file, and directed a letter to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing inviting the Province to meet community advocates about a provincial rezoning decision {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved the official plan and zoning changes for a 24-storey mixed-use building with 415 rental units, as amended {{vote:m7}}.
The zoning for 70 Fountain Street East will allow rooftop mechanical equipment up to 6 metres, replacing the staff-recommended 4.5-metre cap {{vote:m4}}.
Short-term bike parking at 70 Fountain Street East must include at least 15% larger spaces for bigger and accessible bikes, on the private portion of the site {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Community hub and affordable housing proposal
decisions.detail: Council asked the proponent for a public written draft proposal, after which staff will hold exploratory talks and report back, on a cost-neutral basis to the City {{vote:m8}}.
The City Clerk was authorized to publish and serve notice of intention to designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m1}}.
Council received staff report 2026-275 on the City-initiated amendments {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On 70 Fountain Street East, the developer's team argued that a 24-storey building needs rooftop mechanical space of about 6 to 6.5 metres, and said more room can improve energy efficiency. Staff said other downtown buildings fit within 4.5 metres and noted concerns about appearance. Council settled on up to 6 metres.

On bike parking, councillors pressed for wider spaces for accessible bikes and cargo bikes. The developer offered 15% larger spaces. Staff had not assessed bike racks on the city boulevard, so the amendment kept them on private land.

On the community hub, one councillor said the idea was worth exploring, citing hundreds of possible affordable homes. Others worried about costs to Guelph taxpayers, water capacity, and a site outside city limits. The CAO said staff would not act until the proposal is public, and that water capacity would likely be the limiting factor.

On the Niska lands, many delegates urged council to restore open space and parkland. They disputed the GRCA's account of why the land was bought, questioned how public the 2012 change was, and said the parcel matters for forest, groundwater and parkland. Staff said the designation was tested at the OMB, there is no planning rationale to change it, and the land is farmed and was not part of the former park.

Staff and the CAO warned that the landowner's lawyer reserved the right to take legal action, and that the pending transfer of about 126 acres of former waterfowl park lands could be at risk. Councillors said they would support the withdrawal to protect those lands while pursuing the Province. A delegate lawyer disputed the financial risk, saying agricultural use would continue as a legal non-conforming use.
